title: Mic the three singers by the 3:1 rule
instruction: Take the red, green and blue mic stands out of the grey case and stand each one upright on the table within 6 cm of the singer marker of the same colour, with every two mic stands at least 3 times as far apart as the larger of their two distances to their own singers.
context: When several voices are close-miked, each mic is kept at least three times as far from every other mic as it is from its own source, so a neighbour's voice reaches it much quieter and later than its own and the mixed channels don't comb-filter into a hollow, phasey sound. Setting each mic straight in front of its singer breaks the rule here. Done by: sound engineering technicians, audio and video technicians, live-sound stagehands.
setup: A wooden table, its top 1.10 m front to back and 1.30 m side to side, 74.75 cm above the floor. The two arms stand on it facing forward, 19 cm in from its back edge, their bases 61 cm apart: 30.5 cm left and 30.5 cm right of the table's centre line. 'In front of the arm bases' is measured forward from the line through the two bases; 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view. Three singer markers are fixed to the table in a row across it, their centres 28 cm in front of the arm bases: painted wooden cylinders 6 cm in diameter and 4 cm tall, red 12 cm left of the centre line, green on it, blue 12 cm right of it (12 cm apart, centre to centre). An open dark grey plastic mic case is fixed to the table in front of the left arm, its centre 20 cm in front of the arm bases and 33 cm left of the centre line (2.5 cm further left than the left arm's base): inside 17 cm front to back and 7 cm side to side, a 5 mm floor and 5 mm thick walls 2 cm tall. Three mic stands stand upright in the case in a row along its length, 33 cm left of the centre line: painted wooden cylinders 3 cm in diameter and 8 cm tall, each weighted to 100 g by a 12 mm steel rod set down its axis (about 9 cm³ of steel in 47 cm³ of wood), stand-ins for weighted mic stands; red 14 cm, green 20 cm and blue 26 cm in front of the arm bases. An orange rubber handover pad, 7 x 7 cm and 1 mm thick, is fixed to the table on the centre line, its centre 13 cm in front of the arm bases. Nothing else is on the table. The right arm cannot reach the case. The left arm can set the blue stand itself only on the near side of the blue singer with its gripper low (the simulator's IK reaches 23 cm in front of the arm bases, 12 cm right of the centre line, with the gripper 7 cm above the table, but not 15 cm up), for example with green behind its own singer; handing the blue stand to the right arm, for example by the pad, is another route, and the one the demo takes.
scoring: Distances are between centres, seen from above; d is a stand's distance to the centre of the singer marker of its own colour. A mic is placed when its stand is upright (axis at most 10 degrees from vertical), standing on the table (its bottom within 3 mm of the table top), d is at most 6 cm, and it is nearer its own marker than either other one: 0.1 for each placed mic. For each pair of placed mics: 0.3 for red-green, 0.3 for green-blue, 0.1 for red-blue. All three placed: 1.0. A stand is stowed when its centre is over the inside of the case or over the orange pad, and carried when its bottom is more than 8.2 cm above the table top (higher than the 8 cm top of a standing stand, so a stand stacked on a standing one is not carried); every other stand is a live mic, placed or not, standing, stacked, lying or held low. Stowed and carried stands earn nothing and zero nothing. The score is 0 if any live stand's centre is closer to a placed mic than 3 times that placed mic's d (the 3:1 rule; for two placed mics, they must be at least 3 times the larger of their two d apart). The score is also 0 if any stand has fallen off the table (its bottom more than 3 mm below the table top), or if any stand, including one still held, is tipped more than 10 degrees with its lowest point less than 5 cm above the table top (knocked over, lying or leaning). A stand tilted in a gripper with its lowest point 5 cm or more above the table is not knocked over; whether it must keep the 3:1 rule depends only on the stowed and carried rules above.
reset_notes: Stand the three stands back upright in the case in the order red, green, blue from the near end, 6 cm apart centre to centre, the red one's centre 2.5 cm from the case's near inside wall (1 cm clear of it), the blue one's centre 2.5 cm from the far inside wall. The singer markers, the case and the pad stay fixed (tape or clamp them down).
fidelity: Approximate: a mic is reduced to its stand's footprint; capsule height, aim and pickup pattern aren't modelled, and the singers are fixed markers. The 3:1 rule is the trade guideline against comb filtering, not an acoustic simulation. The stands are rigid cylinders of uniform density. Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than painted wood.
